Title: Dr Mutebi leads Africa's breast cancer fight
NewsSummary: AKU faculty founding member of Africa Breast Cancer Council, promoting early diagnosis
NewsContent:
The delayed diagnosis of breast cancer in Africa is a significant public health challenge, with women often waiting more than six months after noticing symptoms. This delay is often attributed inefficiencies in the healthcare system and limited access to specialized care, resulting in more than half of African women receiving a late-stage diagnosis. Unfortunately, a late diagnosis reduces survival chances and increases the cost of cancer care due to expensive therapies and longer hospital stays.

Dr Miriam Mutebi, a distinguished alumna of the Aga Khan University (AKU) and a breast cancer surgical oncologist at the Aga Khan University Hospital, Nairobi (AKUH, N) is leading the charge in combating this pressing issue. As a founding member of the newly established Africa Breast Cancer Council, she is part of a powerful coalition of African women leaders dedicated to addressing the continent's most prevalent cause of cancer death among women. Supported by Roche, a global biotech company, this initiative brings together oncologists, surgeons, first ladies, advocates, survivors, and other prominent figures to drive change. 

A Pioneering Career at AKUH, N 

As Kenya's first female breast cancer surgeon, Dr Mutebi's career at AKUH, N exemplifies her dedication to improving women's health in Africa. Her expertise and leadership at this renowned healthcare institution contribute significantly to early diagnosis and improved treatment outcomes for breast cancer patients. 

Collective Action for Change 

The Africa Breast Cancer Council aims to address the critical challenges women face in accessing timely and effective breast cancer care. Dr Mutebi recognizes the urgency of this mission. 

"Most African women with breast cancer are diagnosed too late," she emphasizes. "This Council has chosen to launch during Breast Cancer Awareness Month to start raising our collective voice and accelerate action." 

The Council's ambitious goals include: 

  • Reducing the time to diagnosis from six months to just 60 days. 

  • Promoting systemic improvements in healthcare infrastructure, access, and funding. 

  • Encouraging collaboration, improved data collection, and better patient outcomes. 

Dr Mutebi highlights the Council's multi-disciplinary approach, recognizing the need for a comprehensive strategy. "As the work progresses," she explains, "we will be highlighting the critical gaps that different countries in Africa need to close to speed up effective breast cancer diagnosis, treatment, and survivorship."

Dr Mutebi's passion to improving the lives of women across Africa is demonstrated by her efforts to combat breast cancer through the Africa Breast Cancer Council. She is the President of the African Organization for Research and Training in Cancer (AORTIC), past president for Kenya Society of Hematology and Oncology (KESHO) and on the Board of Directors of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC). Dr Mutebi is also the co-founder of the Pan African Women's Association of Surgeons and is part of the Kenya Association of Women Surgeons. Her combined expertise at AKUH, N and her leadership role in this impactful initiative positions her as a true champion in the fight against breast cancer.
